Hi Jonas,

We are starting design reviews for our integration with Redwood and have a couple of items we need to confirm from a compliance perspective before we proceed:

- If we bring our own keys (CMK) via a customer-managed KMS, can key material be pinned to a UK HSM (so tokens are encrypted with a key that never leaves the UK)?
- If Redwood uses its own KMS/HSM for ephemeral keys, how do transfers of key material or metadata interact with the UK Addendum/IDTA requirements? Any cross-border metadata flows could be a blocker for us.
- Can you provide an attestation or diagram showing where key wrapping/unwrapping occurs for requests routed through EU/UK regions?

I've attached a one-page list of our questions (medicore-km-questions.pdf). Legal Ops is copied; they may follow up with more specific wording for contract addenda.

Target: we'd like a short written answer and a proposed mitigation (if needed) by EOD Tuesday so our security review can keep moving.

Thanks,

MediCore Health

Subject: Re: Question — regional KMS/HSM + UK Addendum impact

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, followed by a short proposed architecture and next steps.

Short answers:
- Customer-managed keys: yes — we support BYOK workflows integrating with customer KMS and HSMs. We can configure key wrapping so that unwrapping for token decryption happens only within an operator you control (UK region) if you provision the HSM/KMS there.
- Redwood-managed KMS/HSM: if you use our managed keys, some management metadata (key IDs, rotation timestamps, service audit logs) may be replicated across control plane services. That replication can have transfer implications under the UK Addendum depending on what you classify as personal data or personal data metadata.
- Attestation/diagram: attached (redwood-km-overview.pdf) — shows where wrapping/unwrapping happens and control-plane vs data-plane boundaries.

Proposed mitigation options for MediCore to pick from:
1) BYOK with in-region HSM: customer keeps wrapping keys in their UK HSM; Redwood receives only wrapped tokens and never sees key material. This minimizes transfer risk.
2) Bring-your-own-KMS with tenant key proxy: Redwood proxies requests to your KMS endpoint in-region and never persists unencrypted key material.
3) Redwood-managed with contractual carveouts: we can offer contractual commitments (log minimization + geo-restricted control plane) but will need an exception in the UK Addendum for certain management metadata; legal to confirm.

Next steps I suggest:
- Kimberly: legal angle and whether option 3 requires an explicit UK IDTA clause or if it is covered by current Addendum language.
- Laura: ops to confirm what logs/metadata are replicated and what we can gate behind a contractual commitment.

Sara — I've highlighted the sections in the attached overview that map to your three questions. Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question — regional KMS/HSM + UK Addendum impact

Thanks Jonas — good summary. Important legal notes for the thread (high level):

1) UK Addendum / IDTA scope: The UK Addendum treats certain technical metadata as potentially relevant to international transfer analysis when it can be linked back to data subjects or operationalized to re-identify. We need to be conservative here — if management metadata (rotation timestamps, key IDs tied to tenant IDs) is replicated to control plane servers outside the UK/EU, that may trigger a transfer.

2) Customer-managed keys (BYOK): preferred path. If key wrapping/unwrapping occurs exclusively within a UK-controlled HSM that the customer manages, we would be able to represent to MedicoRE that no unencrypted key material left the UK. We should request: (a) architecture diagram, (b) attestation from customer's KMS/HSM provider, (c) permissible evidence language for our DPA/UK Addendum.

3) Redwood-managed keys: we can offer contractual constraints but cannot reasonably guarantee zero cross-border metadata flow without operational changes. If MedicoRE needs that guarantee, we should offer (i) an operational change request to provide an isolated UK-only control plane for that tenant (possible but will incur cost), or (ii) customer-managed key mandate.

Action items:
- Jonas: please extract the minimal set of metadata fields that our runtime/control plane will emit to dashboards/alerts and confirm whether any contain tenant-identifying values. We can then evaluate whether a contractual log-minimization SLA would be sufficient.
- Laura: pull a sample of control-plane replication topology and list of regions where metadata is replicated.
- Sara / Legal Ops (MedicoRE): please confirm whether BYOK is an option and, if so, whether they can provide an HSM attestation.

Attaching relevant UK Addendum excerpts we typically rely on (uk-addendum-extracts.docx). I will draft suggested phrasing for the DPA if we need to offer option 3.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
